lessonActivities.title: AT - ON - IN Prepositions – Your First Step! 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Hello! Let's explore time prepositions: at, on, and in. These helpful words tell us when things happen in English. 📚

What are they for? At is for exact times, on for days and dates, and in for longer periods like months or years.

PrepositionWhen to UseExamples
AtSpecific times, exact momentsat 3:45 PM, at noon, at sunrise
OnDays, dates, holidayson Tuesday, on September 8, on Christmas
InMonths, years, seasons, parts of dayin June, in 2021, in the morning

Remember: These prepositions are like time labels - choose the right one for clear communication.

Watch out: Don't mix them up, like saying 'in Monday' instead of 'on Monday'.
functions: Identify correct preposition for time expressions
Use at, on, in in sentences
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Practice Tip: Think of time as a line: at for points, on for surfaces, in for spaces.

lessonActivities.title: FOR - SINCE - AGO: Expressing Duration and Past Time 🚀
lessonActivities.content:
Great job! Now let's learn about for, since, and ago. These words help us talk about how long things have been happening or when they happened in the past. 📈

How they work: For shows duration, since shows starting point, ago shows time back from now.

WordWhat it showsExample
ForLength of time (how long)for 10 minutes, for 5 years
SinceStarting point (from when)since 2010, since January
AgoTime in the past (how long before now)2 years ago, 10 minutes ago

Pro tip: Use Present Perfect with since and for when talking about continuing actions.
examples: I have been waiting for 10 minutes.
I have lived in Tokyo since January 2010.
I arrived at the bus stop 10 minutes ago.
Hugo is going to study in Sydney for 6 months.
A lot has changed since his appointment.
The castle was built 300 years ago.
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Memory Aid: For = forward (duration), Since = start (continuing), Ago = back (past).

lessonActivities.title: FOR - DURING - WHILE: Time Relationships 🔍
lessonActivities.content:
Excellent! Let's learn for, during, and while to show how events connect in time. 🎭

What's the difference? These words help us understand relationships between actions.

WordFollowed byMeaningExample
ForLength of timeHow long something lastsfor 10 minutes
DuringNounThroughout an eventduring the summer
WhileSubject + verbAt the same time aswhile I was sleeping

Fun fact: While can also mean 'although', but here it's about time.
examples: I have been standing here for 10 minutes.
During the summer I go to the beach.
While the teacher was speaking, the students took notes.
Tony is going to San Francisco for a week.
Interesting speeches were made during the conference.
You should go to a show while you are in Las Vegas.
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Practice Tip: For + time period, During + noun, While + clause.

quizActivities.question: Which preposition is used for months?
quizActivities.hint: In is for longer time periods like months and years.
quizActivities.explanation: In is used with months, years, seasons, etc.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct sentence with 'since'.
options: I have lived here since 5 years.
quizActivities.hint: Since is used with a starting point and Present Perfect.
quizActivities.explanation: Since indicates the starting point of a continuing action.

quizActivities.question: Which is correct: 'during the movie' or 'while the movie'?
quizActivities.hint: During is followed by a noun.
